thread.title: Growth Stocks Lead Sell-Off; 2 Sectors Buck Drop | Investor's Business Daily

author: DAVID SAITO-CHUNG
title: Growth Stocks Lead Sell-Off; 2 Sectors Buck Drop | Investor's Business Daily
text:
The Nasdaq paced a broad sell-off in growth stocks today , falling more than 2% and poised for its worst day since a 2.1% drop on June 25. Volume is running higher on the all-electronic exchange, indicating heavy institutional selling.
X The tech-heavy composite index also sharply undercut the 50-day moving average for the first time in months. A further drop below the intermediate-term support level would indicate that a more significant pullback is underway.
Besides sharp declines in the FANG stocks, Microsoft ( MSFT ) and Apple ( AAPL ), smaller-sized growth leaders also fell to key technical trading levels.
Align Technology ( ALGN ), pioneer of the Invisalign clear dental braces, dropped more than 4% in fierce turnover to 359.85, slipping below its 50-day line.
Notice on a daily chart how the longtime member of the Sector Leaders list of top growth stocks succeeded in rebounding back above the 50-day moving average during significant pullbacks in late July and mid-August.
Another longtime big winner, Grubhub ( GRUB ), also rolled below its 50-day line in above-normal turnover. Shares in the mobile and online food-ordering service look poised to close below the key support level for the first time since June 27.
Paycom Software ( PAYC ), Ligand Pharmaceuticals ( LGND ) and Veeva Systems ( VEEV ) are piercing or approaching their 50-day moving averages in active trading.
Another sharp sell-off in long-dated U.S. government bonds and news of a possible hacking of circuit boards that went into the products of major U.S. consumer electronics companies spurred heavy profit-taking on Wall Street. The S&P 500 and the Dow Jones industrial average fell around 1.2%.
The small-cap S&P 600 slumped 1.3%, falling further below its 50-day moving average. At 1030, the index is now 6.4% below its all-time high of 1100.
Some Financials Rally Select life insurance and energy-related stocks advanced. Brighthouse Financial ( BHG ) rose more than 1% to 45.92 but remains below its 200-day moving average. Shares are still in the early stages of forming a first-stage base.
Prudential Financial ( PRU ) gained nearly 2% in heavy trading. The giant in life insurance, annuities and mutual funds is trying to overcome upside resistance at its 200-day line.
Higher interest rates generally benefit insurers as they can earn bigger yields on newly bought debt securities. The yield on the benchmark U.S. Treasury 10-year note surged past 3.20% for the first time since July 2011.
Energy Sector Leader New IPO Cactus ( WHD ) rose more than 2% and posted a new all-time high of 40.45. The oil wellhead equipment firm went public in February at 19 a share. The small-cap stock is climbing past a 37.60 buy point in a nearly five-month base.
Near-term U.S. oil futures dropped 2.3% to $74.64 a barrel, but remain up nearly 24% since Jan. 1.
